items.title: Roland Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000
items.q: Mozart also was a guy who loved to make flatted ninths

ctx.x: So when you play Mozart or Beethoven, you’re most likely recognizing the harmonies as they go by.

Yes. All the variations and nuances that are put in. Like for instance in the Appassionata, the last movement, Beethoven is using the diminished chord over a pedal point you know. That flatted ninth that we call today in jazz, that, Beethoven may not have called it a flatted ninth, but he certainly heard it the same way we are hearing it now. And there are certain things that happen in Mozart. Mozart also was a guy who loved to make flatted ninths, but he would move them right away. See they were afraid of…
Right. He couldn’t come out and say what he wanted to.
